operational_definition: An explicit normative stance regarding the ethical dilemma.
An empirical proposition used to support ethical reasoning.
An explicit moral principle, value, duty, or norm supporting the reasoning.
An explicit ethical conclusion derived from the reasoning.
Recognition of an alternative position or objection.
Explicit recognition of competing moral considerations.
Explicit comparison or balancing of competing considerations before reaching a conclusion.
Proposal of a justified course of action.
Explicit consideration of physical or psychological well-being, suffering, harm, or benefit.
Explicit recognition of rights, entitlements, or moral claims.
Explicit concern for fairness, equality, equity, or distributive justice.
Explicit recognition of agency, freedom, self-determination, or informed choice.
Explicit appeal to obligations, duties, accountability, or professional responsibilities.
Explicit recognition of fragility, dependency, marginalization, or the need for protection.
Explicit emphasis on interpersonal relationships, empathy, care, trust, or relational responsibilities.
Explicit recognition that an individual, organism, or entity possesses value independent of its utility.
Explicit concern for the ability to develop, function, or flourish.
Explicit recognition that social, cultural, historical, political, or institutional conditions are morally relevant.
Explicit reliance on empirical data, research findings, or scientific knowledge to support the ethical judgment.
Explicit appeal to professional training, clinical experience, or disciplinary expertise as justification.
Explicit use of philosophical theories, ethical frameworks, or theoretical concepts to justify the judgment.
Explicit appeal to laws, regulations, or formal institutional norms.
Explicit reference to the participant's own lived experience as grounds for the judgment.
Explicit appeal to cultural practices, customs, or tradition.
Explicit appeal to religious doctrine, spiritual belief, or faith-based reasoning.
Explicit use of an analogy or comparison to a different case, situation, or entity to justify the judgment.
Any other explicitly identifiable source of justification not captured by SJ01-SJ08.
